reasons.A: Closest sentence movement: long, clause-stacked sentences joined by semicolons, an opening rhetorical question and the same hedging stance (I suspect, arguably, perhaps); hedges are laid on slightly thickly but stay near the passage's own level.
reasons.B: Right formal, reflective register and first-person hedging, but sentences are shorter and more evenly measured, with no questions or semicolons and a few clipped lines (We seldom do.) the author does not use.
reasons.C: Short, punchy, declarative sentences, list-driven paragraphs and a plain, assertive modern tone; far from the author's long, hedged, periodic style.
